title: Critical-fix escalation, patch-branch strategy, and backport runflow
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Define an actionable, automated-friendly runflow for identification, escalation, patch-branch creation, CI validation, backporting, canary gating, and rollback for critical production regressions and security fixes. This ticket consolidates severity criteria, naming conventions, backport window policy, automated tooling (redwood-backport/redwood-rollout), and operator checklists so on-call and release engineers can execute reliably under pressure.

Severity criteria (decision thresholds):
- Sev-1 (Urgent): production integrity or data loss (customer-facing data corruption, crash loop, or security exploit). Immediate pager, 1-hour response SLA.
- Sev-2 (High): significant feature-blocking regression or major latency/backpressure degrading >30% of customers. Pager or high-priority alert, 4-hour response SLA.
- Sev-3 (Medium): Partial degradation affecting a subset; degrade but functionality intact. Triage during normal hours.
- Sev-4 (Low): Cosmetic or non-urgent; backlog.

Patch branch & tag naming conventions (examples):
- Branch for hotfix on maintained minor: patch/2.3/hotfix-ENG-33641-short-desc-20260312
- Branch for security-only fastpath: security/2.3/CVE-YYYY-NNN/hotfix
- Final patch tag: v2.3.5-hotfix.ENG-33641

Backport policy:
- Supported release channels: current stable minor + 2 prior minor LTSes (e.g., 2.3, 2.2, 2.1). Explicit table of supported versions maintained in RELEASES.md.
- Backport window: security fixes: up to 18 months from the minor release date; critical regressions: 6 months; bugfixes: 3 months. Exceptions require Release Manager sign-off.
- Backport strategy: prefer minimal semantic changes (cherry-pick small commits). If the change diverges, create a 'backport/<target>' branch and include a short compatibility shim and test.

Automation & CI validations:
- New pipeline job 'patch-validate' runs on patch branches: unit tests, selected integration tests, smoke end-to-end on canary infra, and a keystore access smoke test if change touches KMS or auth.
- 'redwood-backport' CLI automates cherry-picks, resolves trivial conflicts (whitespace/renames), creates backport PRs against target branches, and labels PRs with 'backport-requested'. The CLI emits a backport checklist artifact (JSON) that is uploaded to the PR as a comment.
- Merge gating: all backport PRs must pass 'patch-validate' and have approval from Release Manager + one owner of changed module.

Canary gating & rollout policy:
- Canary %: default 5% traffic to patch version for 30 minutes. Metric thresholds to auto-promote: error rate < 1.5x baseline, latency p95 < 1.2x baseline, CPU/GPU utilization within expected variance.
- Auto-rollback triggers: (a) error rate > 2.5x baseline sustained for 10m, (b) latency p95 degradation > 250ms above baseline for 10m, (c) increased OOMs or crashes. When a trigger fires the rollout system pauses and notifies on-call; operators may initiate immediate rollback.

Rollback decision tree (operator steps):
1) Confirm incident & scope using runtime dashboards (routes, customer tokens, sample requests).
2) If rollback thresholds met, identify deployment ID & patch tag.
3) Issue rollback via 'redwood-rollout rollback --tag v2.3.5-hotfix.ENG-33641 --deployment <id>' or via Console rollback button.
4) Validate rollback by monitoring health checks for 15 minutes and sampling failing requests for regression verification.
5) Open a 'rollback follow-up' ticket to surface root cause analysis and backport correctness issues.

Patch branch lifecycle & backport flow (step-by-step):
- Triage & severity classification by on-call.
- Create a minimal repro and attach to ticket.
- Create patch branch using naming convention. Branch includes a short header in the PR body: motive, impact, observed metrics, suggested canary windows.
- Run 'redwood-backport --targets 2.3,2.2 --cherry-pick <sha> --ci'. CLI creates PRs for each target and attaches the patch-validate artifact.
- Release Manager approves; merge into target branches using 'squash' to keep history minimal, then tag patch release using release tool.
- Start canary rollout as defined. If green, promote to 25% for an hour, then 100% after final validation.

Operator playbook & checklists (condensed):
- Hotfix checklist: reproduce -> severity -> branch -> PR-> patch-validate -> RM approval -> canary rollout -> monitor -> promote/rollback -> postmortem.
- Post-merge tasks: increment CHANGES.md, verify telemetry dashboards updated, notify support & customers if public-impacting.

Edge cases & guidance:
- Large refactors: do NOT backport by cherry-pick. Instead, implement compatibility shim in target branch or schedule a coordinated minor release.
- Database schema changes: must include migration-backout plan and cross-team approval; consider blue/green for migrations.
- If patch affects private deployment customers, coordinate with Solutions & Account teams; provide patches for Private appliances per contractual SLAs.

Open decisions & follow-ups:
- (Design) Add a lightweight RBAC guard in redwood-backport to require Release Manager token for cross-minor backports.
- (Infra) Provision a reserved canary pool for hotfixes to avoid noisy neighbors during sensitive rollouts.
- (Tooling) Add an automated backport risk score (based on changed files, test coverage, churn) to prioritise manual review.

Artifacts & links:
- Release playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/release-engineering/hotfix-playbook
- Draft redwood-backport CLI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/redwood-backport
- Canary dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary
- Example PR (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
1) Documented severity table & backport windows committed to RELEASES.md.
2) redwood-backport workflow automated to create backport PRs and upload patch-validate artifacts.
3) Canary gating thresholds implemented in rollout service and exposed in Console.
4) Runbook with concrete rollback commands and operator checklists published and reviewed by Release Managers and Security.

Success metric: reduce time-to-first-patch-merge for Sev-1 incidents from current median (8h) to <= 3h and ensure 95% of hotfix rollouts use the canary gating flow for observable promotion/rollback.
